# T004 — Pin and validate Node.js 24

## Summary
Node v24.21.0 with npm 11.19.0 passes the clean install, build, both workspace suites, and lint. Test discovery remains 35/35 (15 backend, 20 frontend; zero failed or skipped), matching T003.

## Changes
- `.nvmrc`: select major 24 for repository runtime routing.
- `package.json`, `backend/package.json`, `frontend/package.json`: set `engines.node` to `^24.0.0`.
- `package-lock.json`, `backend/package-lock.json`: regenerated metadata through npm 11 `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` (root, then `--prefix backend`). Root lock reflects all three engine pins and npm pruned several unused optional peer entries; backend lock reflects its standalone engine pin. No locked package version or framework was upgraded. Root lock still includes the Rollup Linux native artifact.
- No application, ACS, CI, or deployment code changed.

## Decisions
- Confirmed the Node release schedule on 2026-10-20: Node 24 entered LTS 2025-10-28 and reaches end of life 2028-04-30; Node 26 does not enter LTS until 2026-10-28. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/Release/main/schedule.json .
- Reviewed Node 23/24 release notes (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v23.0.0 and https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.0.0): `require(esm)` became default in 23; Node 24 brings npm 11, new globals, test-runner behavior and API deprecations. Existing ESM applications and suites required no compatibility fix. Kept framework/TypeScript versions and the transitive `@types/node` 22 unchanged rather than making an unrequested dependency/toolchain change; explicit type-check assessment belongs to T014.
- Used `/opt/node/24/bin` first in `PATH` for npm lock updates and all validation commands. No warnings, lint rules or tests were suppressed.

## Validation
- Repository root, `PATH=/opt/node/24/bin:$PATH`, `CI=true TZ=UTC LANG=C.UTF-8`: `node --version` **v24.21.0**; `npm --version` **11.19.0**.
- `npm ci`: passed; four existing deprecated-package warnings (`inflight`, `rimraf`, `glob`, `sudo-prompt`). npm 11 additionally reported install-script approval notices for `@swc/core`, `esbuild` and `keytar`; no approval or script-policy change was made. npm reported 56 affected root package names, reserved for the dependency tasks.
- `npm run build --if-present`: passed; three existing CSS optimizer warnings, unchanged from T003.
- `npm test`: passed **35/35**, 0 failed, 0 skipped (backend 15, frontend 20), matching T003.
- `npm run lint --if-present`: passed; five existing warnings, zero errors, unchanged from T003.
- `git diff --check`: passed; verified the three root-lock engine records, standalone backend lock engine, and Rollup native entry.

## Follow-ups and risks
- npm 11's new install-script approval notices need evaluation in later dependency/tooling work; these are install-time diagnostics, not additional build or lint warnings.
- Existing vulnerability findings and transitive `@types/node` 22 remain; dependency-family remediation is planned in T005–T013 and explicit frontend type-check reporting in T014. No production service or deployment test was run.
